title: The ox forgotten
hookLine: picture seven: home, the ox forgotten, the herder at rest (Ox-Herding 7)
tomorrow: what's left in the picture when even the herder goes?

cards: The first week on a new bike, every pedal takes thought. A year later you ride to the shop and can't remember the ride. Kuoan's seventh picture is that later day.
The herder is home, sitting outside his hut in the sun. He isn't searching, or holding, or riding. He's just sitting.
And the ox is nowhere. Not lost this time. Forgotten, because there's nothing left to manage.

teach.b: The preface explains: there are not two things. The ox was only a stand-in, like a trap set for a hare, or a net for a fish.

teach.h: FORGET THE TRAP, KEEP THE FISH.
teach.b: That echoes Zhuangzi, the Taoist sage, who said that once you have the fish, you can forget the trap.
The verse: the ox is gone, the man sits at peace; the red sun is high, and he's still dozing; whip and rope lie idle under the thatched roof.

teach.h: THE RAFT STAYS ON THE SHORE.
teach.b: The Buddha had his own image for this, in the parable of the raft: you build it to cross the river, and you don't carry it on your head once you're across.
Zen's teaching here: the method serves the way, and it can be set down. At rest isn't laziness. It's the practice finally sitting still inside you.
The preface has an image for it: like gold drawn out of ore, like the moon coming out from behind clouds. Nothing new was made; something was uncovered. Six pictures brought him here.
Searching, alone in the grass. The footprints, found in the teachings. A glimpse, through a bird's song.
It pulls, toward the sweet grass.
The rope, held close every day.

how: Zen students read the seventh picture as the method set down once it has done its work; Buddhists know the Buddha's parable of the raft. People on this path let a rest day be rest.

o: a parable about a farmer who forgot to feed his ox
the seventh picture: home, the ox forgotten, at peace
a festival when oxen rest from plowing for a day

games.q: the week of pictures: tap the pairs.
p: the ox wants the sweet grass

s: in picture seven, the herder has lost the ox again
forgotten, not lost: the preface says there are not two things.
The preface compares the ox to a trap set for a hare
once the hare is caught, you can forget the trap.
in the Buddha's parable, you carry the raft with you after crossing
you leave it on the shore; it was for crossing, not for carrying.

games.q: a man crosses a river on a raft he built, then hoists it onto his head to carry everywhere. what does the Buddha's parable say?
o: leave it on the shore: the raft was for crossing, not for carrying.
carry it always, out of gratitude for the crossing it gave him.
keep it close in case another river shows up someday.
games.why: in the parable of the raft, the Buddha says the wise man leaves it at the shore. Kuoan's herder does the same with the ox: the method can be set down.

practice: Close your eyes for the two minutes, and don't do anything with the breath: no counting, no rope, no fixing. Let the body sit the way the herder sits in the sun.
If you catch yourself checking whether you're resting correctly, that's the ox; let it go too.

wordCard.voice: The ox forgotten: Kuoan's seventh picture. The herder at home, the method set down, nothing left to manage.

orig.note: Chinese: the ox forgotten, the man remains, the title of Kuoan's seventh picture.

carryVoice: Pocket this: at rest, whip and rope idle under the roof. Seven pictures in, and a week behind you.
